rejected.title: Linear and angular motion
card: Linear motion
Movement in a straight line or a curved path, where every part of the body moves the same distance in the same direction. A force (a push or pull) starts or changes it.
Angular motion
Rotation about an axis, a fixed point or line. A torque, which is a force applied away from the axis, starts or changes it.
Speed and velocity
Speed = distance ÷ time and has no direction. Velocity = displacement ÷ time and has a direction. Displacement is the straight-line change in position.
Momentum and impulse
Momentum = mass × velocity. Impulse = force × time. A larger impulse causes a larger change in momentum.
rejected.remember: Force changes linear motion and torque changes angular motion. Impulse changes momentum.

a.q: Which description fits a torque acting on a gymnast on a high bar?
opts: A force applied away from the axis that causes rotation
A force through the body that causes linear motion
The product of the gymnast's mass and velocity
The distance travelled divided by the time taken
a.why: Torque is a force applied away from an axis, so it causes rotation. A force that does not act away from an axis is linked to linear motion, not rotation, and mass × velocity is momentum, not torque.
a.clue: Torque needs an axis to turn around.

b.q: Priya, a netballer, pushes on the ground for a longer time with the same force when she jumps. What is the effect on her momentum as she leaves the ground?
opts: Her change in momentum is larger, as impulse is larger
Her change in momentum is the same, as force is the same
Her change in momentum is smaller, as contact is longer
Her change in momentum is larger, as her mass is greater
b.why: Impulse = force × time, so the same force over a longer time gives a larger impulse and a larger change in momentum. The same force does not mean the same change, because time also counts, and her mass has not changed.
b.clue: Impulse depends on force and on time.
